correctness.rationale: In characteristic two, xy+yx is the Lie bracket. For A trivial, center Z is C2^r and K=kZ has the squarefree basis t_T with t_i=1+z_i. The raw spans split by quotient coset and are K-stable by moving any central coefficient into the first entry of a left-normed bracket. A bracket reaching v from u acquires the factor 1+∏z_i^{B_i(u_i,v_i)}, up to a central unit. Its support is in the ideal I_{S(v)} generated by nonzero coordinates of v, and degree is at least one. At level two each such t_i is achieved by choosing one coordinate of the commutator vector. Thus the induction gives only degree at least n−1 at level n, and only monomials meeting S(v). In the converse step for target support T of size at least n, take i in T∩S(v) and j in T other than i. Choose commutator vector supported exactly on i, yet u_j≠0: use u_j=v_j when v_j≠0, and otherwise any nonzero vector. Then t_{T−{i}}h_u is available at level n, and the next bracket gives t_T h_v after removal of its central unit. This proves the coset formula, including the zero coset and empty sums. For support size j there are 4^r−4^{r−j} eligible cosets; the last nonzero degree consists of 4^r−1 top monomials. Tensoring with kA multiplies dimensions by |A| even when A has even order: the other tensor factors may all be taken equal to 1 in the reverse inclusion. The independent binary group-table and elimination replay checks every coset rank for r=1,2,3 and every mixture up to permutation, including (512,387,243,63,0) for rank three. The proof, not the finite computation, covers arbitrary r and all characteristic-two fields.
residual_risks: No extension to arbitrary class-two groups or to associative-ideal dimensions. Central commutator coordinates must split as stated.

evidence: arXiv:2611.06587v1 §§3–4, including Theorem 4.3, concerns the index and supplies a sufficient criterion covering these products for r≤7 (j=r+1≤8). arXiv:2610.10915v1 §1, Theorem 7.5 and the upper dimension subgroup recursion on p. 10 give index coverage over the prime field for all ranks here: D_(2)=H′ has r elementary central directions, D_(3)=1, so the index formula gives r+2.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The lower generated ideal vanishes exactly when its generating raw bracket span does, so index coverage is genuine. For this family general field and abelian-factor cases follow from scalar extension and tensoring with the commutative group algebra. These facts do not determine dimensions of any raw layer before vanishing.

evidence: Index agreement is forced because the lower ideals are generated by the raw spans. The second raw dimension is already a standard conjugacy-class count: the quotient by additive commutators has one basis class per conjugacy class, and there are |A|·5^r classes. But index and degree two do not give intermediate monomial supports.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Do not credit L1, L2 or the index as new discoveries by themselves. The exact lower central filtration and its invariance across mixtures is stronger than these consequences; standard upper ideal information includes monomials in cosets that the raw formula excludes.

value.rationale: The support formula gives actual raw homogeneous subspaces in a natural class of modular group algebras. It shows precisely how the vanishing of commutator coordinates affects every intermediate layer and why dihedral and quaternion squares do not alter these ranks. This is useful for distinguishing lower central structure from nilpotency indices or generated-ideal dimensions, already inequivalent in the first nontrivial example.
residual_risks: Exact for this direct-product family; does not identify the algebras with one another.
